docstring:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$ whenever
$|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure $\gamma_n(K) \geq 0.99$.
Does $10K$ contain a compact convex set $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 0.01$?
references: Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:
type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (K : Set (ℕ → ℝ)),
    IsCompact K →
      Balanced ℝ K →
        0.99 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf K →
          ∃ C, IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ 10 • K ∧ 1e-2 ≤ Green54.gaussianMeasureInf C
